chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who arrives in Mecca and the heat becomes intense for him, so he performs Tawaf around the Kaaba and delays Sa'i until it cools down. He said: 'There is no harm in that, and perhaps I did it.' He said: 'And perhaps I saw him delay Sa'i until the night.'

key_terms.السَّعْي: Sa'i, the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.الطَّوَاف: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.الْحَرُّ: Heat, specifically intense heat affecting ritual performance
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it, a legal ruling indicating permissibility
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, the holy city where the Kaaba is located

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to delay Sa'i until night due to heat during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of delaying Sa'i to avoid extreme heat, even noting it as part of his own practice, which highlights the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship) in ritual worship. This ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the sequence of Hajj rituals when health or comfort is at stake, prioritizing the completion of the act over rigid chronological order. The Imam’s personal example serves as a strong evidentiary basis for following the Imams' practical application of the law in varying environmental conditions.
